text: In March 2026 the 22's wait rose about half a minute and has stayed up. Most of it is buses bunching more, and missing buses doubled. No other line rose, not even the others that left Potrero Yard with it on 14 February, so we don't know why
note: Pre-send gate round 3 (2026-11-15): weekday excess wait 1.318 min in January, 1.759 on 1 to 13 February (other lines rose too), 1.379 on 14 to 28 February, 1.978 in March and 1.873 in April; every other line 1.290 to 1.359 in March, and the other Potrero Yard lines (14, 30, 49, 5, 5R) show no March step. Missing buses rose from 0.183 to 0.397 min. The yard move on 14 February is a plausible cause of more missed runs [inference — mine]; confirming it needs SFMTA's missed runs by line and cause, which it doesn't publish. Rechecked under the 10-minute rule (pre-send gate round 4, 2026-11-15): excess wait 1.349 in January, 1.752 in February, 1.991 in March, 1.843 in April; missing buses 0.234 to 0.392, a quarter of the rise.

text: Our speed for the 49 starts here: before April 2022 it left out the Van Ness stretch, whose old stops have no distance in our table, so it read faster than the whole line ran
note: Pre-send gate round 6 (2026-11-15), verified 5: trip_time.py takes stop-to-stop distances from 511 months from 2023-01 on; 22 of the 49's 82 weekday stop pairs in January to March 2022, all on Van Ness (stop codes 16473, 16798 to 16834, 17736, none in the current stops.txt), had none and were dropped. From April the BRT station codes 18088 to 18105 are in the table (80 of 81 pairs). On the stop-pair parquet the line fell 8.40 to 7.82 mph March to April 2022, but the 57 pairs measured every month January to June fell only 8.42 to 8.22: about two thirds of the step is Van Ness entering the measure. Other lines show no step that month (14 8.43 to 8.37, 22 6.09 to 6.06). Opening: SFMTA blog, 31 March 2022, 'Tomorrow, April 1, we will cut the ribbon on San Francisco's first Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) corridor on Van Ness Avenue.'

text: From 16 April 2022, 511 tracked more of Muni's scheduled trips in frequent hours, on some lines, so part of the missing buses before then is buses 511 didn't track
note: Pipeline review of 1e8a8062 (2026-11-17), rechecked on data/muni-ewt/daily/2022-*.csv the same day: observed over scheduled frequent-hour departures, 1 March to 15 April against 16 April to 20 November 2022, rose on the 1 (0.635 to 0.908), 14R (0.554 to 0.810), 30 (0.614 to 0.844) and 49 (0.706 to 0.875), and stayed flat on the M (0.961, 0.945), N (0.944, 0.939), KT (0.951, 0.944), 24 (0.897, 0.924) and 5R (0.891, 0.890); all lines 0.791 to 0.857. SFMTA's service hours delivered ran 82 to 99% a month over 2022 (service_delivered.csv), with no step on either date, so the step is tracking, not service [inference — mine]; the check that would confirm it is SFMTA's own missed-run counts by line for those months, which it doesn't publish.

text: From 21 November 2022, 511 tracked more of Muni's scheduled trips in frequent hours on most lines, so part of the missing buses before then is buses 511 didn't track
note: Same review and recheck: all lines 0.857 (16 April to 20 November 2022) to 0.945 (21 November to 31 December); among others the 14 0.888 to 0.958, 22 0.874 to 0.960, L 0.855 to 0.952, cable cars 0.44 to 0.48 rising to 0.82 to 0.91, with the M (0.945, 0.950) and KT (0.944, 0.954) flat. The missing-bus share of the frequent-hour wait before this date is partly untracked buses [inference — mine].
